title: trim build images, unify lint adapters, and add toolchain-manifest for hermetic builds
author: Jordan Lee
release_notes: Reduces CI build image size and surface area, unifies lint adapters across repos, introduces toolchain-manifest for reproducible builder images. No API changes.
commits: 2b3c4d5: adopt slim base-images for node/python builders
3c4d5e6: migrate lint entrypoints to unified adapter with feature flags
4d5e6f7: remove legacy makefile targets and devDeps pruning script
5e6f7g8: update CI executor config and cache warm hooks
changed_files: tools/toolchain-manifest.json (new - pinned tool versions for reproducible images)
ci/workflows/presubmit.yml (switch to unified lint job, smaller matrix)
docs/dev/build-images.md (updated with manifest and upgrade instructions)
description:
Context and motivation:
This PR is part of the CI hygiene and build tooling sprint (ENG-4821). Our CI images had gradually grown: redundant apt layers, unpinned tool versions, and divergent lint entrypoints across repositories. That caused slower cold-starts, larger cache foot-print, and surprising transitive devDeps in CI. The goal here is threefold: 1) reduce build image size and layer count; 2) provide a single lint adapter so tool upgrades/flags are consistent; 3) introduce a declarative toolchain-manifest to make builder images reproducible and auditable.

What I changed (summary):
- Introduced tools/toolchain-manifest.json: pins node/npm, pip, black, eslint, golang, and bazel/protoc versions used to bake images. The manifest drives the image bake and the lint adapter.
- Trimmed Dockerfiles for node/python builders: collapsed RUN layers, removed unused apt packages, switched to distroless-slim / manylinux-slim bases where appropriate. Image sizes reduced ~28% on average in local measurements.
- Added a small Go-based lint adapter (tools/ci/adapters/lint-adapter) which standardizes invocation across repo roots and supports feature flags for legacy linters. This replaces ad-hoc bash wrappers that differed between services.
- Removed legacy Makefile targets and a pruning script that attempted to remove devDeps at runtime; instead we bake hermetic images driven by toolchain-manifest.
- CI changes: presubmit job matrix slimmed (tests split into fast/slow lanes), unified lint job used in all presubmit workflows, cache warm steps moved earlier to avoid repeated downloads.

Checklist:
- [x] Tool versions pinned in toolchain-manifest.json
- [x] Lint adapter added with unit tests and feature-flag toggles for fallback
- [x] Dockerfiles updated and smoke-built in CI images pipeline (local build verified)
- [x] Docs updated with migration/runbook (docs/dev/build-images.md)
- [x] QA: presubmit ran successfully on a subset of active repos

Performance/impact notes:
- Average node builder image size: 1.1GB -> 780MB (local Docker build, uncompressed layer sum)
- Cold CI job start times improved ~20% observed across small sample of flaky runners
- Cache footprint reduced since we moved language tool installs into image bake rather than per-job installs

Testing and CI:
- All presubmit checks passed in the final run (unit + integration smoke + lint).
- I've included a short smoke CI in a fork that replicates the baked image verification step; the pipeline uploads an SBOM artifact so infra can validate exact tool versions.

Review conversation synopsis:
- Asha asked for a migration path for services still using the old bash wrappers. Reply: the lint adapter includes a --compat flag and CI workflows will toggle a feature flag for 2 weeks; a follow-up cleanup task (ENG-4890) will remove compat when adoption hits 100%.
- Miguel requested the manifests be validated at CI-time. I added a lightweight validator that fails fast if the manifest has missing required entries; validator lives under tools/ci/manifest-validate and is run as part of image-bake job.
- Evelyn noted we should keep an escape hatch for ad-hoc tooling during incident response; I documented the fallback command in docs/dev/build-images.md and left the old wrappers available under tools/legacy-wrappers for 30 days.

Follow-ups and TODOs:
- ENG-4890: Rollout compat flag and delete legacy wrappers after adoption window.
- Add image SBOM verification as part of the infra promote pipeline (tracked in ENG-4902).
- Consider cross-repo rollout for unified lint adapter in redwood-examples and sdk repos (will open separate PRs).

Rollout and merge:
- Merged to main via squash merge after approvals from Asha and Miguel and green CI.
- Feature toggles in presubmit workflows enabled for all repositories in the org by a small coordinated push (infra change pushed in a separate PR).

Notes for oncall/incident responders:
- If presubmit fails due to missing toolchain entry: run tools/ci/manifest-validate against the manifest; error message includes required key and suggested version.
- To temporarily revert lint adapter to legacy wrapper: set the LINT_ADAPTER_MODE env var to "legacy" in the CI job or fallback to tools/legacy-wrappers/<repo>-lint.sh.

Longer rationale (engineering):
Unifying the lint entry point drastically reduces cognitive load for code reviewers and maintains consistent linter output, which is crucial for automated formatting and CI automation. Baking tools into images brings deterministic CI, lowers flakiness from remote registries, and reduces per-job network variance. The toolchain-manifest provides an auditable single source of truth for developer tooling versions and is intended to be consumed by image bakes, local devcontainer builds, and the lint adapter so the same versions are used everywhere.

If any team wants a longer walkthrough or image size diffs for their repo, ping me and I can export per-repo artifacts or run the local smoke builds on request.
